sentence_stem: I don't have many friends in this city, so
correct_completion: I often feel lonely on weekends.
full_sentence: I don't have many friends in this city, so I often feel lonely on weekends.
acceptable_variants: I spend a lot of time at home.

options.text: I have a lot of parties every week.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the first clause. A person with few friends does not usually have many parties, so it cannot be the result.

options.text: I often feel lonely on weekends.
I always have many people to talk to.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts 'I don't have many friends', so it cannot be the logical result that 'so' introduces.

options.text: I like the city very much.
options.why_wrong: This is a separate opinion. It does not follow as a result of having few friends, which is what 'so' needs.

grammar_focus: Quantifier 'many' in negative sentences and result clauses with 'so'
explanation: 'So' introduces a result of the first clause. The quantifier 'many' in a negative sentence means few friends, so the logical result is a feeling such as loneliness. Portuguese speakers may expect a contrast after this kind of clause, but 'so' always signals a consequence.
translation: Eu não tenho muitos amigos nesta cidade, então eu frequentemente me sinto sozinho nos fins de semana.
